text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging eng-oncall — p99 streaming latency breached for tenant 'Helicon' (us-west-2). Metric spike detected at 2025-05-12T16:11:05Z. Linking dashboard: https://mon.redwood/aro/alerts/1749821465

amelia (oncall-sre): ack. I see p95 ~ 1.2s, p99 ~ 5.2s on the streaming path for Helicon over the last 10m. Errors up ~3% and stream stalls reported. Starting triage.

rik (eng-runtime): grabbing logs from the streaming proxies and dispatcher. Quick query: `sum(rate(streaming_response_time_seconds_bucket{tenant="helicon",region="us-west-2"}[5m]))` — shows a heavy long-tail at >3s.

jun (eng-ml): Helicon's workload has a lot of long prefixes + repeated function calls. Could be KV-cache thrash on single-tenant instances. Any recent model rollouts pinned to large context?

amelia (oncall-sre): no model rollouts in last 24h for Helicon. Checking autoscaler: their dedicated pool is at 95% utilization.

sara (devex): customer reported interactive stalls in support ticket #8452: they see the stream hang after ~2-3 tokens for some prompt patterns.

mike (cust-success): flagged Helicon as high-impact (billing tier: enterprise). I'll notify account and ask them to pause non-critical traffic if possible.

amelia (oncall-sre): first mitigations: 1) enable fallback routing for Helicon to the next available pool in us-west-2 with spare capacity, 2) temporarily lower max-concurrency on their pool from 40->20 to reduce queueing, 3) switch streaming -> chunked non-streaming for in-flight requests if stall persists. Applying now.

rik (eng-runtime): running commands:
```
# move route for tenant
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP" https://api.redwood/routes/migrate \
  -d '{"tenant":"helicon","from_pool":"helicon-prod","to_pool":"shared-usw2-2"}'

# restart proxy pods for tenant pool
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/helicon-proxy
```

amelia (oncall-sre): applied route migration, rolling restart started. Watch pod restarts and connect success.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollout for helicon-proxy: 3/3 updated, 3/3 available (16:19 UTC).

jun (eng-ml): still seeing p99 ~ 2.1s after migration but streaming stalls reduced. KV-cache hit-rate for Helicon dropped from 92% -> 40% during spike. That aligns with a long-prefix workload causing cache eviction/rehits.

rik (eng-runtime): temp mitigation suggestion: enable aggressive prefix caching for Helicon (increase cache TTL, avoid evicting on LRU). Pushing a config change now.

amelia (oncall-sre): changed cache TTL to 10m for Helicon. Also backpressure: set `max_inflight_per_tenant=25`.

sara (devex): posted a quick recipe to Helicon: if you can batch repeated tool calls or reduce repeated long metadata in prompt it will help; sending as suggested mitigation.

mike (cust-success): Helicon acknowledged, will throttle automated job that was ramping up at 16:02 UTC. They reported a large customer test run that coincides with our spike.

amelia (oncall-sre): current numbers 16:35 UTC: p95 820ms, p99 1.9s, errors back to 0.8%. Streaming stall reports dropped 90%. Recording these for postmortem.

jun (eng-ml): root-cause hypothesis: combination of unusual long-prefix prompt patterns + a sudden synthetic load from customer test -> KV cache thrash + queueing in streaming hotpath -> tail latency. Longer-term fixes: pin a per-tenant cache reservation, smarter prefetch for repeated prefixes, and fallback policy to a less-streaming-sensitive model class under load.

rik (eng-runtime): opened PR for per-tenant cache reservations (RFC-1723). Also adding monitoring to alert earlier on cache hit-rate drop for dedicated pools.

amelia (oncall-sre): impact summary for handoff: Helicon affected ~18k requests over 35m window; estimated SLO breaches: p99 target 800ms, observed peak p99 5.2s for 12 minutes. Customer saw interactive stall reports but no data loss. Mitigations applied: route migration, restart proxies, increased TTL, lowered concurrency.

mike (cust-success): I updated Helicon and requested a confirm when they're unblocked. They said interactive flows are OK now, will keep us posted.

amelia (oncall-sre): preparing handoff to Lee (oncall-next). TL;DR: issue likely KV cache thrash tied to long-prefixed prompts + customer test spike. Immediate mitigations applied and system stable. Please continue monitoring p95/p99 and cache hit-rate.

lee (oncall-next): taking over. Thanks for the summary — I'll keep the alert channel open and coordinate with eng-runtime for follow-ups.

incident-bot: incident created: INC-2025-512-helicon-latency. Severity: Sev2. Add postmortem label when triage complete.

amelia (oncall-sre): adding quick notes for postmortem: timeline, metrics (p95/p99 series), KV-cache hit-rate graph, routing migration, proxy restart, customer test confirmation. Assigning owner: rik (eng-runtime) + jun (eng-ml).

rik (eng-runtime): I'll collect traces and stack dumps from the period 16:00-16:20 and attach to the incident.

jun (eng-ml): I'll run evals on the Helicon prompt set against our cache-aware runner to reproduce the thrash pattern.

sara (devex): I'll draft a short post-incident note for Helicon with suggestions and a checklist for avoiding test-run spikes.

mike (cust-success): Thanks all. Marking customer as notified.

lee (oncall-next): closing paging loop. If anything regresses ping me directly. :white_check_mark:
